title: Steady Rollout SLA Scenario Planner
content:
Purpose:
This is a working planner for a 'steady rollout' launch pattern that prioritizes SLA preservation and predictable operator load. Use for late-stage beta -> gradual ramp to 100% over weeks. The doc mixes a quick decision heuristic, staffflow simulations, KPI snapshot, plus throttle triggers and contingency actions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API features (new model route, new model family, or major config change) and dedicated deploys where customer-visible latency/cost matters.
- Goal: protect 99th percentile latency SLO and error budget while enabling feature exposure to cohorts.
- Time horizon: 0-30 days post-activation.
- Primary constraints: GPU capacity, token-backend concurrency, oncall headcount.

Quick decision heuristic (one-line):
- If p99 latency > target OR error-rate > baseline + 2x stdev -> throttle to previous traffic band and trigger the ops cascade. Otherwise proceed with next cohort.

Staffflow simulation notes (informal):
- Operator model: 1 L2 engineer + 1 SRE per 2500 active users (30rps sustained), with a 2hr mean time to triage on first alert during day hours. Night coverage: 1 SRE on-call for entire product suite.
- For a 3-cohort rollout (5%, 20%, 100%) expected incident load per cohort: cohort1 ~ 0.3 paged incidents/day, cohort2 ~ 1.2/day, cohort3 depends on amplification. Plan to schedule L2 coverage around cohort windows.
- Quick staffing plan: schedule L2 overlap for cohort1 window (2x normal), ensure SRE on-call has playbook link, and stand up a 2-hr war-room for cohort2 if metrics show >10% deviation across KPIs.

KPI snapshot (use as quick reference, this is not the canonical spreadsheet):
- Primary KPIs:
  - p50 latency: target 60ms (baseline 55ms)
  - p95 latency: target 240ms (baseline 200ms)
  - p99 latency: target 520ms (baseline 420ms)
  - error rate (4xx+5xx combined): target <0.5% (baseline 0.2%)
  - unit cost per 1k tokens: target <= $0.90 (baseline $0.78)
  - successful inference throughput (requests/sec): target 14k for peak cluster

- Secondary signals:
  - Queue depth (avg per worker): <40
  - KV cache hit rate: >65%
  - Autoscaler cooldown ratio: normal range 0.8-1.2
  - Customer-facing anomalies reported: 0 ideally; >1 triggers comms plan

Launch readiness checklist (handy quick-run items):
- [ ] Canary traffic validated for 48h with automated integration smoke tests
- [ ] Post-deploy synthetic suite passed (latency & correctness) in ap-south and eu-west regions
- [ ] Observability: dashboard (per-route p50/p95/p99, errors, cost) live and shared link in incident playbook
- [ ] Alerts tuned (p99 > threshold, error-rate spikes, queue depth) and owners assigned
- [ ] Rollback and fallback model pinned and smoke-tested
- [ ] Support and CS playbook: templated responses drafted and reviewed by CS lead
- [ ] Legal/compliance sign-off done for private/de-identified datasets (if applicable)
- [ ] Billing and quota gating rules applied for beta customers
- [ ] Canaries configured to fall back to baseline model on degraded performance

Throttle policy (numeric triggers and actions):
- Soft throttle (triggered automatically): when p99 latency > 1.25x target for 3 consecutive 5m windows -> reduce cohort traffic by 50% via router policy for 15 minutes and mark ticket in PRODOPS-4827.
- Hard throttle (manual): when error rate > 1% sustained for 10 minutes OR p99 > 2x target -> immediate traffic cut to 10% and notify SRE, Product PM, and Customer Success.
- Ramp resume: hold for minimum 30 minutes after soft throttle, validate KPIs during that window (p99 within 1.05x target, errors return to baseline) before increasing by single-step cohort band.

Contingency playbook (short form):
1) Low-severity anomalies: open issue, add to next-day ops triage, non-blocking.
2) Medium: page SRE and L2, create an incident channel, enact soft throttle, escalate to product if regression tied to model change.
3) High-severity: enact hard throttle, engage exec comms if customer-facing SLA breach likely, roll back to previous model or route, trigger postmortem template.
